title: kVp, mA, time: inside the X-ray tube
topic: mA sets how many electrons, time how long, kVp how hard each hits (max keV = kVp, plus more photons); ~99% of the energy becomes heat.

claims.claim: Toy model / schematic: tube-head cutaway (filament in a focusing cup, tungsten target on a copper anode, aluminum filter, collimator); blue dots = electrons, green wave packets = X-ray photons; not to scale
claims.source: Seibert JA. J Nucl Med Technol 2004;32(3):139-47 (PMID 15347692) - full text: thermionic emission, tube current = electrons crossing the gap. Drawing is original and schematic

claims.claim: ~99% heat (gauge needle follows kV x mA; no units shown)
claims.source: Zink FE. Radiographics 1997;17(5):1259-68 (PMID 9308113) - abstract: 1% to X-ray photons, 99% to heat (diagnostic tubes in general). kV x mA (x s) heat unit: Seibert 2004 (PMID 15347692) - full text

claims.claim: mA -> how many: more electrons, more photons, same energies (4 -> 8 mA, values illustrative)
claims.source: Seibert JA. J Nucl Med Technol 2004;32(3):139-47 (PMID 15347692) - full text; McCollough CH. Radiographics 1997;17(4):967-84 (PMID 9225393) - abstract: quantity proportional to tube current

claims.claim: kVp -> how hard: each electron hits harder; max keV = kVp (60 -> 70 kVp, values illustrative)
claims.source: Seibert JA. J Nucl Med Technol 2004;32(3):139-47 (PMID 15347692) - full text: electron kinetic energy (keV) = tube voltage; maximum X-ray energy (keV) set by the peak voltage (kVp)

claims.claim: kVp -> + how many: more photons; output ~ kVp squared (electron count unchanged)
claims.source: McCollough CH. Radiographics 1997;17(4):967-84 (PMID 9225393) - abstract; Nickoloff EL, Berman HL. Radiographics 1993;13(6):1337-48 (PMID 8290728) - abstract: output increases by approximately the square of the tube potential

claims.claim: kVp up: less image contrast (swatch change exaggerated)
claims.source: European Commission. Radiation Protection 136: European guidelines on radiation protection in dental radiology. 2004, sect. 4.1 - guideline full text. Caveat: 60 vs 70 kVp had minimal effect on CMOS sensors in one phantom study (Pita de Melo D et al. Dentomaxillofac Radiol 2026, PMID 42538829 - abstract)

claims.claim: Time -> how long: same beam, on longer; mAs = mA x s (0.10 s -> 0.80 mAs, 0.20 s -> 1.60 mAs at 8 mA; values illustrative, slow motion)
claims.source: McCollough CH. Radiographics 1997;17(4):967-84 (PMID 9225393) - abstract: quantity proportional to exposure time; Seibert 2004 (PMID 15347692) - full text: mAs

claims.claim: Toy model / schematic: spectrum on the scope = Kramers shape x 2 mm aluminum; right-hand end = kVp (60 -> 70 keV), height doubles with mA, hump stays near 30 keV; no vertical scale, no characteristic lines drawn
claims.source: Toy model built for this reel (NIST aluminum attenuation coefficients); not a measured dental spectrum. End point = kVp: Seibert 2004 (PMID 15347692)

claims.claim: Toy model / schematic: the aluminum filter stops the low-energy photons and the collimator trims the beam
claims.source: European Commission. Radiation Protection 136 (2004), sect. 4.2 - guideline full text: filtration preferentially removes lower-energy photons. Proportions in the animation follow the toy model, not a measurement

claims.claim: Cheat sheet: mA -> how many (same energies); kVp -> how hard + how many (max keV = kVp, output ~ kVp squared); time -> how long (mAs = mA x s)
claims.source: McCollough 1997, Radiographics (PMID 9225393); Seibert 2004, J Nucl Med Technol (PMID 15347692). On-screen source line: McCollough; Zink, Radiographics 1997 - Seibert, J Nucl Med Technol 2004 - EC RP136 2004

caption:
3 knobs. What does each do inside the X-ray tube?
mA = how many: hotter filament, more electrons, more photons, same energies.
kVp = how hard: max photon energy (keV) = kVp, and output rises ~kVp². Higher kVp = less contrast (minimal for 60 vs 70 kVp on CMOS sensors in a phantom study).
Time = how long: same beam, on longer. mAs = mA × s.
~99% of the energy becomes heat.
Schematic animation, illustrative settings.
Refs: McCollough 1997, Zink 1997, Radiographics; Seibert 2004, J Nucl Med Technol; EC Radiation Protection 136 (2004); Pita de Melo 2026, Dentomaxillofac Radiol
